question: If the gold foil in the Geiger-Marsden experiment were replaced by a solid sheet of frozen hydrogen, why would large-angle backscattering not be observed?

options.A: Hydrogen atoms are too small to be hit by alpha particles.
options.B: Hydrogen nuclei are negatively charged and would attract the alpha particles.
options.C: The mass of a hydrogen nucleus is less than the mass of an alpha particle, so the alpha particle would push it forward rather than rebounding.
options.D: Hydrogen does not have a nucleus.
